# Jubilees Chapter 7 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QJub (Hebrew fragments) | **Section:** Noah's Instructions; Ham's Sin; Noah's Curses; Division of Earth

---

**7:1** And in the seventh year of this week I planted a vineyard on the mountain on which the ark had rested, named Lubar, one of the Ararat mountains, and it produced fruit in the fourth year, and I guarded its fruit and gathered it in this year in the seventh month.

**7:2** And I made wine from it and put it into a vessel, and kept it until the fifth year, until the first day of the first month.

**7:3** And I celebrated the day of this feast with joy, I and my sons before me, and I drank of the wine on this day.

**7:4** Now on this day I celebrated and rejoiced, I and my sons before me, but Canaan saw that I was in liquor and he came and took hold of me and made a mock of me and covered not his shame before me, but left me lying naked and went his way.

**7:5** And Ham his father saw the nakedness of his father Noah, and went and told his two brothers outside.

**7:6** And Shem and Japheth took a garment and arose, the two of them, and went backwards and covered the shame of their father, and their faces were backwards, and they saw not the nakedness of their father.

**7:7** And Noah awoke from his sleep and knew all that his younger son had done to him, and he cursed his son and said: "Cursed be Canaan; an enslaved servant shall he be unto his brothers."

**7:8** And he blessed Shem, and said: "Blessed be the LORD God of Shem, and Canaan shall be his servant."

**7:9** "God shall enlarge Japheth, and God shall dwell in the dwelling-places of Shem. And Canaan shall be his servant."

**7:10** And Ham knew that his father had cursed his younger son, and it displeased him greatly.

**7:11** And Noah slept with his fathers, and was buried on Mount Lubar in the land of Ararat.

**7:12** Three hundred and fifty years did he complete after the flood; and all the days of his life were nine hundred and fifty years, and he died.

**7:13** And in his life on earth he excelled the children of men save Enoch because of the righteousness wherein he was perfect. For Enoch's office was ordained for a testimony to the generations of the world, so that he should recount all the deeds of generation unto generation, till the day of judgment.

**7:14** And in the twenty-ninth jubilee, in the first week, in the beginning thereof Arpachshad took to himself a wife and her name was Rasu'eja, the daughter of Susan, the daughter of Elam, and she bore him a son in the third year in this week, and he called his name Kainam.

**7:15** And the son grew, and his father taught him writing, and he went to seek for himself a place where he might seize for himself a city.

**7:16** And he found a writing which former generations had carved on the rock, and he read what was thereon, and he transcribed it and sinned owing to it; for it contained the teaching of the Watchers in accordance with which they used to observe the omens of the sun and moon and stars in all the signs of heaven.

**7:17** And he wrote it down and said nothing regarding it, for he was afraid to speak to Noah about it for fear he would be angry with him on account of it.

**7:18** And in the thirtieth jubilee, in the second week, in the first year thereof, he took to himself a wife, and her name was Melka, the daughter of Madai, the son of Japheth, and in the fourth year he begat a son, and called his name Shelah; for he said: "Truly I have been sent."

**7:19** And in the thirty-first jubilee, in the first week, in the second year thereof, Shelah took to himself a wife, and her name was Mu'ak, the daughter of Kesed, his father's brother, in the thirty-first jubilee, in the fifth year thereof.

**7:20** And she bore him a son in the fifth year thereof, and he called his name Eber: and he took unto himself a wife, and her name was 'Azurad, the daughter of Nebrod, in the thirty-second jubilee, in the seventh week, in the third year thereof.

**7:21** And in the first year of the thirty-third jubilee she bore him a son, and he called his name Peleg; for in the days of his birth the children of Noah began to divide the earth amongst themselves, for this reason he called his name Peleg.

**7:22** And they divided it secretly amongst themselves, and told it to Noah.

**7:23** And it came to pass in the beginning of the thirty-third jubilee that they divided the earth into three parts, for Shem and Ham and Japheth, according to the inheritance of each, in the first year in the first week, when one of us was sent to instruct them.

**7:24** And he called his sons, and they drew nigh to him, they and their children, and he divided the earth into the lots which his three sons were to take in possession, and they reached forth their hands and took the writing out of the bosom of Noah their father.

**7:25** And there came forth on the writing as Shem's lot the middle of the earth which he should take as an inheritance for himself and for his sons for the generations of eternity, from the middle of the mountain range of Rafa, from the mouth of the water from the river Tina, and his portion goes towards the west through the midst of this river, and it extends till it reaches the water of the abysses, out of which this river goes forth and pours its waters into the sea Maat, and this river flows into the great sea.

**7:26** And all that is towards the north is Japheth's, and all that is towards the south belongs to Shem.

---
*EMET notes: Ham's sin in Jubilees (v.4) involves Canaan, not Ham himself — "Canaan saw" vs. Gen 9 where Ham sees. This shifts the curse to Canaan directly. Kainam (v.14-16) = a figure not in MT Genesis but in LXX Gen 10:24 and 11:12-13; he transmits the Watchers' astrological knowledge. The lot-division (v.24) is formalized as a written covenant.*
